papers.title: Kinematically controlled FDM stringing of suspended anisotropic microfiber scaffolds for standardized 3D tissue engineering
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional microenvironments with defined geometry and anisotropic architecture are essential for studying cell behavior and engineering tissue models that reflect native extracellular organization. Recent work has shown that molten stringing in fused deposition modeling (FDM) can be used to fabricate ordered polymer microfiber networks. However, broader application in standardized 3D cell culture is still limited by insufficient process parameterization, incomplete kinematic description of fiber drawing, and a lack of digitally transferable toolpath strategies. Here, we establish a kinematically quantified and digitally parameterized FDM-based workflow for generating suspended anisotropic PLA microfiber architectures with controlled spatial organization. Using a customized high-speed CoreXY printer, experimentally determined motion limits were related to the theoretical process window defined by acceleration, velocity, and travel distance. In parallel, mathematically defined toolpaths were implemented through a Python-based FullControl workflow, enabling programmable control over fiber orientation, spacing, anchoring positions, layer organization, and non-extrusion drawing movements. Under defined drawing conditions, suspended PLA microfibers with diameters of 39.8 ± 3.5 µm were reproducibly generated and assembled into multilayer anisotropic constructs with predictable spatial architecture. Mechanical testing confirmed consistent tensile behavior, with failure occurring within the homogeneous fiber segment rather than at anchoring regions. In proof-of-concept experiments, surface activation and fibronectin coating enabled cell adhesion, supporting fibroblast and motoneuron-like cell attachment within the suspended architectures. Overall, this work advances FDM-based microfiber stringing from a fabrication phenomenon to a reproducible, kinematically defined, and digitally transferable platform for standardized anisotropic 3D microenvironments in biofabrication, mechanobiology, and in vitro model systems.

papers.title: Treatment strategy for patients with end-stage hip disease and ipsilateral intertrochanteric fracture: 1-stage or 2-stage total hip arthroplasty?
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The optimal treatment strategy for patients with ipsilateral intertrochanteric fracture and pre-existing end-stage hip disease requiring total hip arthroplasty (THA) remains unclear. PURPOSE: This study aimed to compare perioperative surrogate markers, clinical outcomes, and radiological outcomes between 1-stage and 2-stage THA. METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort study reviewed 75 patients, including 42 who underwent 1-stage THA shortly after intertrochanteric fracture onset and 33 who underwent initial internal fixation followed by secondary THA after fracture union. Perioperative surrogate markers, clinical outcomes, radiological outcomes, and complications were compared between the 2 groups. RESULTS: No femoral stem revision, radiographic loosening, or reoperation-related mortality occurred in either group during follow-up. During the arthroplasty procedure, 1-stage THA required longer operative time (120 [53] minutes vs. 90 [25] minutes), greater intraoperative blood loss (400 [200] ml vs. 300 [200] ml), and greater transfusion requirement (transfusion rate: 42.9% vs. 21.2%; transfusion volume: 500 [400] ml vs. 400 [200] ml). Because femoral canal preparation and stem insertion during 1-stage THA occupied the proximal femoral space required for fragment reduction, this group had poorer fracture reduction quality (optimal reduction: 14.3% vs. 42.4%) and inferior early postoperative function, as reflected by lower Harris Hip Scores and higher WOMAC scores. However, clinical outcomes did not differ between the 2 groups after 1 year. Intraoperative periprosthetic femoral fracture and postoperative stem malalignment were more frequently observed in the 2-stage THA group. CONCLUSIONS: 1-stage THA enables fracture management and hip reconstruction in a single operation but may involve longer operative time, greater blood loss, and higher transfusion requirements during the arthroplasty procedure, as well as poorer early outcomes. 2-stage THA offers a more elective setting for arthroplasty after fracture union but requires an additional operation and carries specific risks during secondary THA, including intraoperative periprosthetic femoral fracture and femoral stem malalignment.

papers.title: Postoperative CT-detected occult acetabular fracture after primary cementless total hip arthroplasty: incidence and exploratory associated factors
papers.abstract: Occult acetabular fracture during press-fit cup insertion in primary total hip arthroplasty (THA) may be underrecognized because it is not identified intraoperatively and is often not visible on routine postoperative radiographs. Occult acetabular fracture is likely affected by multiple implant-related and clinical factors, including cup design, fixation strategy, and acetabular morphology. This study aimed to describe the incidence of postoperative computed tomography (CT)-detected occult acetabular fracture after primary cementless THA and to explore clinical and implant-related factors associated with fracture occurrence. We retrospectively reviewed a consecutive single-surgeon series of patients who underwent primary cementless THA between March 2023 and December 2025 with postoperative CT evaluation. Occult acetabular fracture was defined as a fracture not recognized intraoperatively and not visible on routine postoperative radiographs but confirmed on postoperative CT. Acetabular cups were categorized as standard-profile or low-profile cups. Age, sex, body mass index, cup profile, and primary diagnosis were compared between the fracture and no-fracture groups. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed as exploratory analyses. A total of 284 hips were included. Occult acetabular fracture was identified in 15 hips (5.3%). The incidence was 4.3% in the standard-profile cup group and 9.8% in the low-profile cup group. Low-profile cup use was associated with occult fracture in the multivariable model (odds ratio, 3.74; 95% confidence interval, 1.05 to 13.39; p = 0.042). Age, sex, and body mass index were not significantly associated with occult fracture. Compared with primary osteoarthritis, secondary osteoarthritis was not significantly associated with occult acetabular fracture in the multivariable model (odds ratio, 4.42; 95% confidence interval, 0.68 to 28.90; p = 0.121). Postoperative CT-detected occult acetabular fracture occurred in 5.3% of hips after primary cementless THA. Low-profile cup use was associated with occult fracture in the multivariable model, but this finding should be interpreted cautiously because cup profile, implant system, and fixation strategy were closely linked, and the number of fracture events was small. Secondary osteoarthritis was not significantly associated with fracture occurrence after adjustment in the present cohort, and a subgroup analysis suggested that this may relate to diagnostic heterogeneity within the category, with most fractures occurring in ankylosing spondylitis-related hips. These findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and may help guide future studies incorporating standardized CT protocols, objective bone-quality measures, detailed fracture morphology, and clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Bionic skin with hair follicle regeneration capability from acoustic fluids-mediated 3D printing
papers.abstract: Tissue engineering holds substantial potential for constructing normal skin with appendages such as hair follicles, directly restoring skin’s complete physiological functions. The current challenge lies in recreating biomimetic hair follicle organs with high-level cell density and architecture. Here, we developed an acoustofluidic-assisted 3D bioprinting platform to fabricate bionic skins with efficient hair follicle regeneration capability. Pre-formed hair follicle germs, derived from co-cultured epidermal and dermal mesenchymal stem cells, were encapsulated within a hydrogel bioink. Controlled acoustic fields generated flow vortices that directed cell migration and promoted organized cellular assembly from initially disordered states. Guided cell aggregates were then patterned through bioprinting to construct a grid-structured bionic skin. This architecture provided stable 3D support while maintaining high porosity, enabling efficient gas exchange. The printed bionic skin exhibited well-organized spatial cell distribution, high cellular viability, and promising differentiation potential. Further in vivo experiments demonstrated the efficiency of the bionic skin in accelerating mature hair regeneration, showing promise for clinical alopecia treatment.

papers.title: Engineering 4D Motion in Biofabrication Using Natural Polymers
papers.abstract: Abstract The development of 4D materials has opened new possibilities for biomedical engineering by moving beyond static constructs toward systems capable of dynamically interacting with biological environments. Unlike conventional materials, 4D systems can undergo programmed shape changes over time in response to external stimuli, more closely mimicking the adaptive, dynamic nature of native tissues. These changes can be reversible, referred to as shape-memory, or irreversible, known as shape-morphing, depending on the underlying mechanism. In the first case, materials transition between a temporary deformed shape and their original shape in response to a certain stimulus. In the second case, the material forms a new shape after stimulation, and its initial configuration cannot be restored. Triggered by physical, chemical, or biological cues, these dynamic responses offer opportunities for the development of smart biomedical platforms. This review highlights the growing use of natural-derived materials, such as alginate, collagen, and chitosan, among others, in the design of 4D systems. Particular emphasis is given to the different types of stimuli that can govern these changes in conformation, to the biofabrication strategies used, and to mechanisms that underlie them. Furthermore, current and emerging biomedical applications for these smart materials are discussed, with a focus on tissue engineering approaches and controlled drug delivery, underscoring the potential of natural-based 4D materials to advance the next generation of biofabricated therapies.

papers.title: An Automated AI-Based Framework for Rapid Progressive Collapse Assessment of Steel Frames
papers.abstract: Abstract Progressive collapse remains one of the most critical failure mechanisms in multi-story steel structures, whereby the loss of a single structural element can trigger disproportionate failure of the surrounding system. Although international design guidelines increasingly require explicit collapse-resistance evaluation, practical implementation remains limited due to the high computational cost and modelling complexity of nonlinear finite element (FE) analysis. This study presents an automated artificial intelligence-based framework for rapid progressive collapse assessment of multi-story steel moment frames, jointly predicting the Load Increase Factor (LIF) and Dynamic Increase Factor (DIF) without repeated nonlinear FE analysis. The specific contribution of this work is threefold: (1) a large-scale parametric database generated through a factorial study spanning five geometric and configurational parameters, number of stories, story height, bay span, number of bays, and column removal location, producing 10,962 unique base building configurations, structured as 32,886 configuration–scenario records, each jointly labelled with LIF and DIF; (2) a systematic benchmarking of seven machine learning algorithms and four deep neural network architectures, evaluated on a configuration-level data split in which all load scenarios of a configuration remain in the same partition, and selected through an overfitting-aware criterion rather than validation accuracy alone; and (3) the identification and validation of two accurate surrogate models, a gradient-boosting model (LightGBM) and a compact deep neural network with three hidden layers of decreasing width and rectified linear unit activations, that predict LIF and DIF directly from frame geometry and loading. The deep neural network (DL-3 Deep) achieved the highest test-set accuracy, with coefficients of determination of 0.9714 (LIF) and 0.9576 (DIF) and mean absolute percentage errors of 2.90% and 3.51%, while LightGBM achieved comparable accuracy (0.9664 and 0.9535) as the best classical benchmark. The deep neural network was accordingly deployed as a publicly accessible, web-based decision-support platform that returns predictions in a fraction of a second. Comparison with six held-out FE configurations spanning the validated domain gave mean absolute deviations of 3.76% (LIF) and 3.74% (DIF) for the deep neural network. These findings highlight the feasibility of data-driven surrogate modelling as a practical, deployable surrogate for rapid preliminary progressive-collapse screening within the validated parameter domain, rather than a general replacement for simulation-intensive assessment.

papers.title: Functional 3D-bioprinted hPSC-derived cardiac patches enhance cardiac repair following ischemia-reperfusion injury
papers.abstract: Myocardial ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury is a leading cause of heart failure, as reperfusion therapy restores blood flow but does not replace necrotic myocardium or prevent further remodelling. Myocardial regeneration relies heavily on cardiomyocytes derived from human pluripotent stem cells (hPSC-CMs). Multiple studies have demonstrated that custom-engineered cardiac tissues or organoids can show a resemblance to functional recovery after an infarction. Several reviews have analysed the overall developments in scaffold-based tissue engineering, cardiac organoids, and stem cell differentiation and associated technologies. But most of them have failed to consider how these technologies function in the oxidative, inflammatory, and hypoxic environment that characterizes the I/R injury. According to recent studies, 3D bio-printed cardiac patches improve graft retention, vascularisation, and electrical coupling. However, the mechanisms by which design parameters (bioink composition, oxygen diffusion, electromechanical alignment, etc.) confer resistance to reperfusion stress remain unclear. Despite these promising developments, significant translational obstructions remain unanswered, such as Immature hPSC-derived cardiomyocytes, insufficient vascularization, restricted long-term engraftment, immunological compatibility, and large-scale manufacturing, all of which limit the therapeutic applicability of modified cardiac patches. Thus, successful cardiac regeneration will require not only enhanced biofabrication technology but also pathophysiology-guided design methodologies capable of overcoming the adverse post-ischemic environment. To fill this gap, this review focuses on how the molecular mechanisms of myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury, such as oxidative stress, inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, calcium overload, hypoxia, and adverse remodelling, can be directly translated into the logical design of bioactive cardiac patches that can overcome these pathological barriers, in contrast to earlier reviews that provide a general overview of cardiac tissue engineering. Consequently, we hope this associating study proposes a disease-specific framework that would allow the biofabrication of clinically relevant cardiac patches that incorporate cardioprotective processes, such as metabolic reprogramming, mitochondrial preservation, and paracrine signaling. This review emphasizes a link between pathophysiology-informed bioprinting for functional myocardial healing and generic cardiac architecture.

papers.title: Short Expandable-Wing Suture Anchors for Tibial Eminence Avulsion Fracture Fixation: Effects of Solid Versus Additively Manufactured Lattice Wings on Biomechanical Performance and Cytocompatibility
papers.abstract: Fixation of tibial eminence avulsion fractures (TEAFs) in skeletally immature patients requires adequate mechanical stability within a limited insertion depth to minimize the risk of physeal injury. Conventional transosseous cortical-button fixation (TCBF) requires the creation of tibial bone tunnels, whereas conventional suture anchors may have excessive insertion depths. In our previous study, a short expandable-wing (SEW) suture anchor (9.5 mm in length and 5.5 mm in diameter) with CNC-machined solid wings was developed to enhance fixation strength within a limited bone volume. In the present study, a second-generation SEW anchor was developed by replacing the solid wings with 3D-printed Ti6Al4V lattice wings to provide a potentially more favorable bone–implant interface. The mechanical performance of CNC-SEW and metal additively manufactured SEW (MAM-SEW) anchors was evaluated using polyurethane-block pull-out testing and a porcine TEAF model with single- and double-suture TCBF controls. Cytocompatibility was assessed using an MG-63 direct-contact MTT assay. Pull-out loads were 574.8 ± 10.6 N for CNC-SEW and 501.2 ± 39.2 N for MAM-SEW, compared with 429.0 ± 29.0 N for a historical TWINFIX comparator. After 200 loading cycles in the porcine model, cumulative displacements were 0.9 and 0.7 mm for CNC-SEW and MAM-SEW, respectively, compared with 2.2 and 1.3 mm for single- and double-suture TCBF. The corresponding ultimate failure loads were 278.88 and 292.56 N for the SEW groups, compared with 109.86 and 223.56 N for the TCBF groups. The MAM-SEW group also exhibited higher MG-63 metabolic activity than the CNC-SEW group. These findings demonstrate favorable initial fixation performance and preliminary cytocompatibility of the lattice-wing SEW anchor, supporting its potential application in TEAF fixation. Further studies are required to evaluate long-term osseointegration and physeal safety.

papers.abstract: The longevity of implant-supported rehabilitations largely depends on how masticatory forces are distributed across the peri-implant structures. Overload and imbalance of these loads are associated with marginal bone loss, component fracture, and impairment of esthetics and function, which shortens the lifespan of the treatment. This article aimed to analyze the influence of the distribution of peri-implant biomechanical forces on the success and durability of implant-supported treatments. An exploratory bibliographic review was carried out, consulting scientific articles and specialized books recognized in the field, selected by peer review and relevance to the topic. The analyzed literature shows that a balanced distribution of loads preserves marginal bone and favors osseointegration, whereas implant misalignment, bending forces, and occlusal misfits increase the risk of failure. Bone quality, the presence of keratinized mucosa, and periodic maintenance also proved decisive for long-term stability. It is concluded that planning based on biomechanical analysis, precise occlusal adjustment, and systematic postoperative follow-up are decisive measures to extend the longevity of implant-supported rehabilitations.

papers.title: Protein Corona Selectivity on Carbon Nanotube Biosensors Is Driven by Surface Coating and Chirality
papers.abstract: Abstract Semiconducting single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) are versatile near-infrared fluorophores that can be engineered to create sensors for biological research and diagnostic applications. SWCNT properties depend on both surface functionalization and underlying lattice structure, defined by the chiral indices (n,m), enabling the development of wavelength-tunable nanosensors. While the principles of specific SWCNT surface modification with biomacromolecules are well studied, the impact of SWCNT surface chemistry and chirality on protein interactions in complex biological fluids remains underexplored. Here, we investigated the role of SWCNT surface coating and chirality in protein corona formation using mass spectrometry-based proteomics. We systematically compared protein corona formation in human blood plasma across single-stranded DNA (ssDNA)- and PEG-phospholipid-coated SWCNTs, as well as across nanotube chiralities spanning (6,4) to (9,4). Our findings indicate that surface coating identity is the dominant factor governing differential protein adsorption. SWCNTs with high binding stability ssDNA sequences exhibited greater protein-corona selectivity, preferentially enriching apolipoproteins and more internally structured proteins, whereas the PEG-phospholipid coating globally reduced, though did not eliminate, protein adsorption. Trends with increasing SWCNT diameter and chiral angle were generally aligned to each other, both associated with preferential adsorption of larger proteins with lower secondary-structure content, while revealing some distinctive protein-property associations, suggesting (n,m)-dependent interfacial differences. Protein corona formation was further shaped by protein–protein cooperative binding effects in a SWCNT coating-dependent manner. Molecular dynamics simulations provided mechanistic support for the experimental finding that proteins with higher glycine content displayed enhanced binding to (GT)6- compared to (TAT)4-coated SWCNTs through distinct glycine-peptide binding modes. Finally, we observed surface modification-specific fluorescence modulation of SWCNTs upon protein adsorption, impacting functional sensing of dopamine as a model small molecule. These insights provide a framework for the rational design of SWCNT-based sensors for protein-profile recognition in complex biological environments.

papers.title: Predicting spin-crossover behavior in metal-organic frameworks from limited and noisy data using quantile active learning
papers.abstract: Spin-crossover (SCO) metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) hold great promise for sensing, spintronics, and gas-related applications, however, only a small number of SCO-active examples are known among the thousands of MOFs already synthesized. Computational screening enhanced by machine learning offers a powerful route to uncover these hidden candidates much more rapidly than trial-and-error experiments. However, progress is limited by the computational complexity of obtaining accurate adiabatic energy differences, as these typically require separate geometry optimizations for both spin states, a process that is technically challenging, prone to convergence failures, and difficult to automate at scale. To mitigate these issues, we introduce a data-efficient strategy based on Quantile Regression Tree-based Active Learning, designed to navigate large chemical spaces while remaining robust to noisy and scarce labels obtained from unrelaxed geometries. After actively selecting a 200-sized subset of representative MOFs for electronic-structure evaluation, a Random Forest regressor trained on this data accurately identifies SCO-relevant candidates despite label noise, recovering ~ 82% of PBE-defined positives based on relaxed-geometry adiabatic energy differences, with only two false negatives. Negative-control tests further indicate that the model captures chemically meaningful trends. Applying the model to the unlabeled dataset yields a new collection of high-confidence SCO MOFs, which we denote pSCO-105. This work shows that SCO-relevant electronic properties can be reliably identified from limited and imperfect data through smart training-set selection, enabling accelerated screening of SCO MOFs.

papers.title: Real-time control of sustainable data centers: A two-layer model predictive control framework with workload flexibility and heat recovery
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a two-layer model predictive control (MPC) framework for the real-time operation of data centers integrated with on-site photovoltaic generation, battery energy storage, waste heat recovery, and district heating. The upper layer employs scenario-based stochastic optimization to jointly optimize intraday market participation, workload scheduling, and energy management under uncertainty. The lower layer adopts an adaptive tube-based MPC strategy that compensates for short-term disturbances while tracking the dispatch references given by the upper layer. The framework further integrates multi-horizon forecasting to support real-time decision-making. Microservice-based simulation studies under representative clear-sky, overcast, and oversupply operating conditions demonstrate that the proposed framework accurately tracks dispatch plans despite fast photovoltaic and workload fluctuations. Compared with single-layer control strategies, the adaptive lower-layer controller substantially reduces real-time dispatch deviations and the associated imbalance costs. In addition, the proposed framework naturally adapts to seasonal operating conditions and responds to carbon-aware operating signals, offering a practical approach for economically efficient, sustainable, and grid-supportive operation of future data centers.

papers.title: Hierarchical Nonlinear MPC and Super‐Twisting Sliding Mode Control for a Wheeled Biped Robot Under Uncertainties
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This paper presents a hierarchical control framework integrating nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) with super‐twisting sliding mode control (STSMC) for wheeled bipedal robots. While these platforms offer both wheeled efficiency and legged versatility, their unstable underactuated dynamics and sensitivity to modeling errors pose significant control challenges. The proposed three‐layer architecture employs a high‐level NMPC for trajectory generation, a higher‐frequency STSMC for robust tracking with finite‐time convergence, and whole‐body control for wrench‐to‐torque mapping. Simulation results on the 8‐DoF Tron‐1A platform demonstrate superior disturbance rejection: The framework recovers from 100 N lateral impulses that destabilize baseline NMPC, reduces orientation errors by up to 80% on rough terrain with 0.1 m elevation changes, and eliminates steady‐state errors under 20% actuator degradation with joint friction. These results validate the hierarchical NMPC‐STSMC architecture for achieving robust wheeled bipedal locomotion under significant model uncertainty and external perturbations.

papers.title: A Carbon Break-Even Framework for Computational Generative Design: Formulation and a Proof-of-Concept on Real CAD Geometries
papers.abstract: Computational generative design, including topology optimization and AI-assisted text-to-CAD tools, is promoted as a route to lighter, lower-carbon products, yet the electricity of the design computation itself is rarely counted. This study proposes a carbon break-even framework that adapts the indifference-point concept from computer-hardware sustainability analysis to product redesign, defining a break-even production volume, a net environmental return, and a carbon return on investment within a cradle-to-gate boundary. As a computational proof of concept, a three-dimensional SIMP topology-optimization solver instrumented with CodeCarbon redesigned 20 CAD geometries from the Fusion 360 Gallery under a generic load case, primary aluminum, CNC machining, and an imposed 30% volume reduction. Under these assumptions, all redesigns broke even before one unit was produced (median 0.016 units; maximum 0.39) while retaining, for the analyzed load case, the stiffness of 13 of 14 comparable original parts. Sensitivity analyses show that this outcome is conditional: break-even within one unit no longer holds for every part with recycled aluminum (18 of 20 parts) or for mass reductions below about 12%, the break-even volume grows by over four orders of magnitude with larger meshes or other computational backends, and the saving reverses when the redesign requires laser powder bed fusion.

papers.title: Multi-Field Synergy and Anti-Synergy Mechanisms in Enhanced Heat Transfer Tubes: Angle-Based Characterization and Comprehensive Performance Evaluation
papers.abstract: To advance the systematic understanding of synergy and counter-synergy effects in multi-field synergy theory and to address the gap in applications coupling physics-informed neural network methods with multi-field synergy analysis, this study investigates the coupling relationships among vectors in fluid physical fields based on the conservation equations of momentum, energy, and mechanical energy, thereby elucidating the intrinsic connection between multi-field synergy mechanisms and enhanced heat transfer. With a helical groove tube and a novel irregular-shaped tube as the research objects, computational fluid dynamics and a physics-informed neural network were jointly employed to provide an in-depth analysis of synergy and counter-synergy effects in multi-field synergy theory and to quantitatively characterize the synergy effect. On this basis, a comprehensive evaluation criterion grounded in multi-field synergy theory was proposed to assess the overall heat transfer performance of different heat transfer tubes. The results show that, according to the multi-field synergy principle, a clear mapping exists between the multi-field synergy angles and key evaluation indicators, including flow resistance, heat transfer performance, and energy consumption. Moreover, under conditions where experimental validation of field synergy is not feasible, the overall deviation between the field synergy angles reconstructed by the physics-informed neural network and the computational fluid dynamics results was of the order of 10−1, indicating that this method is highly feasible for cross-validation and auxiliary assessment of computational fluid dynamics predictions and can serve as a concise and efficient alternative approach. In addition, the irregular-shaped tube outperformed both the helical groove tube and the smooth circular tube in terms of flow resistance, heat transfer performance, and energy consumption, with the average optimization percentages of the modified performance evaluation coefficient and modified effectiveness evaluation coefficient reaching 2.03% and 7.82%, respectively. This study provides a theoretical basis and an evaluation framework for the enhanced heat transfer design of different heat transfer tubes and demonstrates important practical value.

papers.title: IoT and GPS-Based Fault Detection in Electrical Distribution Networks Using Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Faults on electrical distribution networks are usually found through manual patrols, which delays the restoration of supply. This paper presents an Internet of Things (IoT) and GPS-based system that detects, classifies and locates faults on an 11 kV distribution feeder using machine learning. The feeder was modelled in MATLAB/Simulink, and five fault types were simulated at selected feeder locations with different fault resistances. Statistical and difference features were taken from the three-phase voltage and current signals, and five models were trained and compared: Decision Tree, Bagged Trees, Support Vector Machine, Artificial Neural Network and Physics-Informed Neural Network. Bagged Trees gave the best balanced result, with 90.74% accuracy for fault type, 96.00% for fault location and an average of 93.37%. This model was built into a MATLAB graphical user interface, which maps the predicted feeder section to GPS coordinates, uploads the result to the Ubidots cloud platform and sends an email alert with a Google Maps link. The results show that machine learning and IoT monitoring can be combined to find and locate faults on distribution lines. The system was tested on simulated data only, so validation with field measurements is recommended.

papers.title: Resources-and Energy-Optimal 5G Slicing: Joint PRB Allocation and Power Control Via Entropy-Guided Cyber Twin Architectures
papers.abstract: The exponential growth and increasing complexity of 5G networks present significant operational challenges that traditional rule-based management systems struggle to handle effectively. However, many existing approaches do not adequately capture traffic uncertainty, which limits their ability to adapt in highly dynamic network environments. To address this, The study proposes an optimized 5G Network Entropy-Guided Cyber Twin architecture to address these limitations. The methodology centers on the application of information-theoretic Shannon entropy to quantify traffic uncertainty across temporal, spatial, and service dimensions. This is executed through a tripartite framework: first, a traffic entropy model is developed to provide a mathematical foundation for uncertainty quantification; second, a Cyber Twin environment is constructed to serve as a high-fidelity virtual replica of the 5G network for safe and efficient policy testing; and third, a Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) reinforcement learning agent is designed to incorporate these entropy measures directly into its reward function. This integration allows the agent to make adaptive, data-driven resource allocation decisions that account for underlying traffic variability. Together, these components enable the joint optimization of resource allocation, power consumption, and system latency. The entropy-guided Cyber Twin framework achieves a total system throughput of 146.8 Mbps through optimized Physical Resource Block (PRB) allocation while maintaining a mean energy efficiency of 0.78 Mbits/Joule by utilizing 75.4% of maximum power capacity. Driven by entropy-augmented state representations within the agent, this predictive resource and power management successfully balances high-performance slicing demands with sustainability across dynamic network conditions.

papers.title: Preparing dental students for safe, effective local anesthesia: a multimodal, evidence-based approach
papers.abstract: Teaching local anesthesia is an essential component of dental education, requiring the integration of anatomical knowledge, psychomotor skills, and clinical decision-making. This narrative review aims to critically examine the main strategies used to teach local anesthesia to dental students, discussing their advantages, limitations, and current level of scientific evidence. A non-systematic literature search was conducted in health-related databases, including PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, LILACS, and SciELO, using combinations of the terms local anaesthesia, dental education, simulation-based training, virtual reality, and dental students, with no date restrictions. Studies published within the last decade were prioritised, as well as recent systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and umbrella reviews related to the topic, and Google Scholar was used as a complementary source to identify potentially relevant studies. Traditional methods remain fundamental to the development of clinical competence, while educational technologies (mobile applications, serious games, augmented reality, virtual reality, and haptic simulators) favor active learning, anatomical visualization, repeated practice, and increased self-confidence. However, most studies show considerable methodological heterogeneity and prioritize subjective outcomes, and evidence on the transfer of these skills to patient care and their long-term retention remains limited. Current evidence suggests that a multimodal approach, integrating conventional methods with digital technologies, represents the most promising strategy for teaching local anesthesia. Nonetheless, multicenter studies with robust methodological designs and objective clinical outcomes are still needed to guide the incorporation of these tools into undergraduate curricula.

papers.title: Multi-Field Coupled Degradation and Life Prediction of Low-Temperature Corrosion-Resistant Steel: A Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) Approach
papers.abstract: In cold regions, steel highway bridges face severe risks of low-temperature embrittlement and corrosion degradation under the coupled effects of extreme cold, freeze–thaw cycles, and corrosive media. Conventional periodic inspections and single-parameter monitoring fail to capture the nonlinear material degradation process throughout the entire service life. Taking the novel low-temperature corrosion-resistant steel (HRB400ERE) used for bridge decks as the research object, this paper proposes a full-life-cycle intelligent monitoring and service life prediction framework integrating multi-source sensing and physics-informed neural networks (PINNs). First, low-temperature Charpy impact and alternate immersion corrosion tests confirmed that the novel steel exhibits impact energies of 59.6 J (φ16 mm) and 57.5 J (φ20 mm) at −20 °C, both >27 J, with a DBTT below −25 °C and 72 h relative corrosion rates of 42.5% (<70%), meeting the intended service requirements. Using these measured physical parameters as boundary constraints, an “environment–corrosion–mechanics” coupled digital twin degradation model was established. To overcome the bottleneck of scarce long-term monitoring data in cold regions, the PINN model deeply integrates Faraday’s law of electrolysis, Arrhenius temperature kinetics, and sparse measured data to dynamically predict the trajectories of material cross-section thinning and low-temperature toughness degradation. Results demonstrate that the model achieves a root mean square error (RMSE) of less than 5% in long-term life prediction. This successfully realizes the transition from “passive inspection” to “active predictive maintenance” for low-temperature corrosion-resistant steel in cold regions, providing a theoretical basis for the intelligent operation and maintenance of transportation infrastructure in extreme environments.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-enabled acceleration and enhancement of 4D device printing
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are rapidly emerging as necessary computational paradigms for 4D device printing—the additive manufacturing of structures programmed to dynamically transform their shape, properties, or functions over time in response to external stimuli. Unlike standard 3D printing, which targets static geometric fidelity and steady-state structural properties, 4D printing involves solving a highly non-linear, path-dependent inverse problem across coupled material-geometry-process-stimulus spaces. This commentary presents the central argument that data-driven and physics-informed AI methods are not merely optional optimizations, but mandatory tools required to navigate the temporal multi-physics design space and make 4D printing deterministic, reproducible, and commercially viable. We clearly delineate between methods already empirically demonstrated (e.g., forward surrogate neural networks, convolutional inverse design of metamaterials, active learning for material discovery, and melt-pool defect detection) and methods currently proposed (e.g., autonomous closed-loop digital twins, physics-informed neural ODEs for long-term degradation, and certified explainable AI pipelines for clinical implants). Furthermore, we distinguish the evidence base for static 3D printing (focusing on relative density, void formation, and static residual stresses) from dynamic 4D printing (focusing on spatiotemporal deformation, phase transformation kinetics in shape-memory alloys, rate-dependent hydrogel swelling, and hysteresis). We highlight the unique challenges of 4D printing—specifically, non-linear multi-physics coupling, extreme computational cost, sparse spatiotemporal experimental data, inverse design non-uniqueness, and actuation drift—and demonstrate qualitatively how physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), active learning, deep generative models, and computer-vision digital twins solve these bottlenecks. Finally, we re-emphasize in our conclusion the transformative role of spatiotemporal AI in bridging lab-scale smart materials and production-grade 4D functional systems.

papers.title: PINN framework with enhanced DIF and peak-strain models for rate-dependent dynamic compressive behavior of concrete: insights from SHPB experiments
papers.abstract: Predicting the compressive response of concrete at high strain rates is central to protective design, yet common empirical relations are calibrated over narrow windows and behave unphysically outside them. Revisiting a split Hopkinson pressure bar programme on 40 and 63 MPa concrete (96 solid and annular specimens, 32–299 s−¹), this study develops a physics-informed framework: a monotone stretch-exponential dynamic increase factor (DIF) replacing the rational form, a Hill peak-strain function, and bounded pore-water and Pochhammer–Chree corrections. A physics-informed neural network (PINN) trained under five constraints is compared with six regressors. Across ten splits the closed-form models remain most accurate (R² = 0.82–0.84), with the PINN and Bernstein regression close behind; on this small, one-dimensional dataset added flexibility does not pay. The PINN alone extrapolates admissibly – monotone and bounded to 4000 s−¹ – though this is constraint-driven, not experimentally validated. SHAP attributes 79% of influence to logarithmic strain rate.

papers.title: Distributed model predictive control with adaptive virtual impedance for power sharing and voltage–frequency regulation in AC microgrids
papers.abstract: Accurate power sharing and voltage/frequency regulation are essential for islanded AC microgrids. Unequal feeder impedances and the coupled effects of impedance adjustment, however, make these objectives difficult to coordinate. This paper proposes a distributed model predictive control (DMPC)-based adaptive virtual-impedance strategy for common-bus AC microgrids with predominantly resistive feeders. A coupled fundamental-power predictor links virtual-resistance and virtual-reactance increments to active- and reactive-power redistribution, allowing each distributed energy resource (DER) to jointly optimize both increments for power tracking and sharing. The distributed receding-horizon optimization incorporates adjustment effort, impedance bounds and a sign-dependent linear approximation of predicted apparent-power constraints. Combined with reverse droop and average-voltage restoration, the strategy coordinates active/reactive power sharing and voltage/frequency regulation without a dedicated secondary frequency-restoration loop. OPAL-RT real-time tests demonstrate coordinated operation under load changes, communication-link outage and DER plug-and-play. Extended tests demonstrate robust power sharing and voltage/frequency regulation under variable delays, random packet losses, asynchronous information exchange and short simultaneous link interruptions. In load-change comparisons, reactive-power steady-state error is reduced by 2.6% and 4.6% relative to the DMPC and DAPI-inspired baselines, respectively. Active-power convergence is shortened by 3.67 s relative to DMPC, while reactive-power overshoot is reduced by 17.8% relative to the DAPI-inspired baseline. The later-stage reactive-sharing benefit is retained under a changed load composition without further tuning. Parameter assessments guide weight and horizon selection, while six- and nine-DER cases retain coordinated operation with similar typical per-DER solver times at fixed horizon and neighbor degree.

papers.title: Statistical Air-Quality Assessment Methods
papers.abstract: Air-quality assessment is fundamental for quantifying health risks and evaluating emission-control policies. However, assessing air-quality data is challenging due to strong variability, heavy tails, complex spatiotemporal structures, and meteorological confounding, all of which call for principled statistical methods. This review provides an overview of existing statistical approaches under four themes: trend analysis for detecting systematic changes, extreme value analysis for characterizing high pollution risk, hierarchical models for capturing spatiotemporal dependence, and meteorological adjustment methods for isolating emission-driven signals. A recurring theme is the role of statistical methods in providing not only fitted or predicted concentrations but also uncertainty quantification for policy-relevant assessment under complex dependence and confounding structures. We use air-quality data from North China to illustrate these methods.

papers.title: Perceptions and attitudes of medical interns at five tertiary public hospitals in a city towards the application of 3D Printing Technology in medicine
papers.abstract: Objective The study aims to conduct a survey among medical interns in order to gain insights into the utilization of 3D printing technology in clinical learning. Methods This cross-sectional survey included 506 medical interns from five tertiary public hospitals in Hefei, Anhui Province. A culturally adapted Chinese version of a questionnaire originally developed at the Medical University of Silesia in Poland was used to assess participants’ knowledge and perceptions of 3D printing technology in medicine. Results Male interns were more likely than female interns to have seen 3D-printed medical models. Clinical medicine students had more exposure to 3D printing than nursing students. Medical Imaging students expressed more uncertainty about the feasibility of 3D printing human body tissues compared to other specialties. Anaesthesiology students felt less confident when assessing the safety of 3D-printed implants, in contrast to Midwifery, Clinical Medicine, and Medical Imaging counterparts. Conclusion These survey findings provide insights for integrating 3D printing into medical education, highlighting the need for broader knowledge dissemination within the medical community and emphasizing safety and ethical considerations in 3D bioprinting applications and research.

papers.title: Smart and Hybrid Academic Libraries as Drivers of Financial Literacy and Entrepreneurial Readiness Among Commerce Students
papers.abstract: The transformation of academic libraries through digital technologies has reshaped their role in higher education, particularly in supporting literacy and lifelong learning. Smart and hybrid libraries, which combine physical collections with digital platforms and intelligent services, are increasingly positioned as active learning environments rather than passive information centres. In commerce education, the growing emphasis on financial literacy and entrepreneurial readiness has created a need for learning support systems that extend beyond the classroom. Despite this shift, the contribution of contemporary library services to the development of these competencies among commerce students remains underexplored. This study examines how smart and hybrid academic libraries contribute to financial literacy and entrepreneurial readiness among commerce students. The objectives of the study are to analyse students’ access to and use of digital library services, assess the role of library resources in strengthening financial knowledge, and evaluate the perceived influence of library-supported learning on entrepreneurial awareness and career preparedness. A descriptive research design was adopted for the study. Primary data were collected from commerce students through a structured questionnaire, while secondary data were drawn from scholarly publications, institutional reports, and relevant policy documents. The data were analysed using percentage analysis and mean score techniques to identify trends in library usage and learning outcomes. The results indicate that increased access to digital resources such as e-books, online journals, financial databases, and virtual reference services has a positive influence on students’ understanding of financial concepts and business practices. The findings also suggest that exposure to library-supported entrepreneurial resources enhances students’ confidence, problem-solving abilities, and readiness to explore self-employment and start-up opportunities. The study underscores the expanding role of smart and hybrid libraries as enablers of financial literacy and entrepreneurial competence within commerce education. It highlights the importance of strengthening library infrastructure and services to support skill development and lifelong learning in the digital era. The study offers practical implications for academic librarians, commerce educators, and institutional policymakers seeking to align library services with contemporary educational and career-oriented needs.

papers.title: The use of the Six Thinking Hats activity in nursing education for intestinal stoma care: a mixed-methods study of nursing students’ opinions and evaluations
papers.abstract: The Six Thinking Hats activity helps students evaluate problems from six different perspectives. The aim of the study was to examine students’ satisfaction with the Six Thinking Hats activity and, their opinions and evaluations on the process, and to jointly evaluate these findings. This is a convergent parallel design mixed-methods study, in which quantitative and qualitative components were conducted. The quantitative phase used a one-group posttest-only design. The qualitative phase involved in-depth interviews. The population of the study consisted of students enrolled in a surgical nursing course during the spring semester of the 2023–2024 academic year at a public university ( N = 117). In the course, Six Thinking Hats activity was implemented in education on the care of patients with intestinal stomas. The quantitative phase was completed with 97 students. For the qualitative phase, criterion sampling was used and 14 students participated. A semistructured individual interview form was used in the qualitative phase. The obtained statements were evaluated with thematic analysis. Students reported significantly higher satisfaction with the Six Thinking Hats activity than with the traditional course method (Z = − 5.271, p < 0.001). For the qualitative phase; 4 categories, 10 themes, and 34 subthemes were identified. The categories included emotions about the activity, the skills/abilities utilized during the activity, and the benefits and difficulties of the activity. The categories included emotions about the activity, the skills/abilities utilized during the activity, and the benefits and difficulties of the activity. Active learning activity appeared to support overall satisfaction by fostering individual cognitive engagement and group-level multi-perspective thinking. At the same time, qualitative results showed an expansion by highlighting both individual and group challenges experienced during the process. The qualitative results also showed an expansion with quantitative scores by revealing students’ awareness of stoma nurse’s professional role and stoma care needs. Findings suggest that the activity may have enhanced student awareness of patient care needs and nursing roles. Consequently, addressing the identified individual and group challenges might help educators further leverage the cognitive and emotional potential of this teaching approach. Not applicable.

papers.title: Six Biological Clocks in the Space Economy
papers.abstract: Future space economies will require materials and compounds as well as food, oxygen, and water. Some products can be mined or fabricated from nonliving inputs; others can be produced by organisms whose useful traits arise through growth, metabolism, environmental interaction, and time. This paper refines the Biological Capital Theory of the Space Economy by separating two lags that its single biological stock already contains: the delay before a viable stock yields a specified product (tau), and the delay before harvested capacity is restored (rho). Both belong to the same stock, and neither is a second kind of asset. Six production systems show how differently the two lags behave: slow-growing instrument timber, a culturally valued Chinese hardwood, a CITES-listed timber, resinous agarwood, fungal composites, and microbial fermentation. Building on established forest economics, the decision framework incorporates time to first yield, time to replenish harvested capacity, sustainable yield, survival risk, enabling infrastructure, resource throughput, and destination-specific alternatives. It distinguishes developmental from ecological maturation, and it treats the discount rate as an explicit parameter reported across a range. The paper identifies testable hypotheses, candidate measurements, and conservation obligations. It does not argue that rare terrestrial hardwoods should be grown on the Moon or that biological products always outperform nonbiological substitutes. Its narrower claim is that maturation and replacement times belong in economic evaluations of off-Earth biological manufacturing. **Keywords:** biological capital; maturation time; space economy; biofabrication; forestry economics; biological manufacturing; mycelium composites; conservation; natural capital; space settlement.

papers.title: Feira de estrutura e função do corpo humano: uma estratégia de metodologia ativa no ensino em cursos da saúde
papers.abstract: Human Anatomy and Physiology are foundational disciplines in undergraduate health programs, playing a crucial role in understanding the structure and function of the human body. However, these subjects are often perceived as challenging by students, particularly during the early stages of their academic training, due to the extensive technical terminology and the need to integrate multiple physiological systems. In this context, active learning methodologies have been increasingly adopted as pedagogical strategies to enhance student engagement and promote meaningful learning. This study aimed to present and describe a pedagogical proposal based on the implementation of a Human Body Structure and Function Fair. Students were organized into groups responsible for presenting different body systems, including the cardiovascular, digestive, renal, endocrine, muscular/integumentary, skeletal/articular, respiratory, and nervous systems. Each group planned and conducted educational activities using didactic resources such as posters, models, interactive games, and oral explanations to present anatomical and physiological concepts to the academic community. As an additional engagement strategy, an activity called the “Extension Hours Bingo” was implemented to encourage visitors to interact with different exhibition stands. The fair promoted the integration of theory and practice, stimulated active student participation, and expanded the dissemination of scientific knowledge within the university environment.

papers.title: Concentration-Aware Model Predictive Control for Pressure–Flow Coordination in Slurry Shield Circulation Systems
papers.abstract: Coordinated pressure and discharge-flow regulation is a practical challenge in slurry shield circulation systems because changes in solids concentration modify pipeline resistance and the flow required by a prescribed transport criterion. This paper investigates concentration-aware model predictive control (CA-MPC) for a reduced two-pump hydraulic circulation unit. A four-state nonlinear model describes chamber pressure, inlet and discharge flows, and well-mixed solids concentration. A locally updated prediction model and a concentration-dependent minimum discharge-flow constraint are implemented within an incremental quadratic-programming controller, subject to pump-command, rate, and chamber-pressure limits. Numerical comparisons with feedforward-assisted proportional–integral control and nominal-model MPC consider set-point changes, inlet-concentration variation, excavation disturbances, and a low-flow conflict scenario. A two-factor comparison distinguishes predictor-information updating from transport-constraint scheduling. In the latter scenario, scheduling the modeled minimum-flow constraint reduced sampled threshold-violation duration from 131.5 s to zero, at the expense of increasing flow-tracking root-mean-square error from approximately 14.0 to 48.5 L/s. Predictor-information updating alone did not improve one-step prediction accuracy in the evaluated case, and larger hydraulic mismatch degraded the constraint benefit. In the matched safety case, the proposed dynamic bound and a predeclared fixed-conservative bound both achieved zero sampled model-threshold violations; the dynamic bound reduced flow RMSE from 54.784 to 48.506 L/s. The joint sensitivity study also revealed model-defined violations for the dynamic controller under increased resistance mismatch and threshold slope. These results quantify an engineering trade-off between pressure–flow tracking and model-defined transport limits. Because the hydraulic parameters and transport threshold are not experimentally calibrated, the findings apply to the stated numerical model and do not demonstrate field-scale deposition prevention.

papers.title: Recent Progress of Machine Learning Technology in Gas Sensing and Detection
papers.abstract: Abstract Although gas sensing technologies are widely applied in environmental monitoring, industrial safety, and food testing, their applications remain constrained by several challenges, including cross-sensitivity, long-term drift, environmental interference, and slow response. Machine learning (ML) provides new opportunities for intelligent gas sensing by extracting useful patterns from complex sensing signals and improving gas recognition and quantitative analysis. Adopting a problem-oriented perspective, this review examines recent progress of machine learning technology in gas sensing and detection. First, ML methods used in gas sensing are introduced according to learning paradigms and sensing tasks. The applications of these methods in solving key gas-sensing problems are then discussed. Specifically, extracting multichannel and dynamic response features improves gas discrimination; domain adaptation and active learning can compensate for gas drift, whereas including temperature and humidity signals can reduce environmental interference; early-response analysis enables faster gas detection without waiting for steady-state responses. This review further discusses the challenges that limit the practical deployment of ML-based gas sensing systems. Potential solutions, transferable from intelligent sensing applications in other fields, are introduced to solve data scarcity, edge deployment difficulty, and poor interpretability problems, such as data-efficient learning, lightweight model design, and interpretable modeling. Finally, future perspectives such as biomimetic olfactory systems, embodied intelligence for gas source tracking, and AI-assisted analysis of new gas sensing materials are discussed. This review provides an overview of the recent progress of machine learning technology in gas sensing, highlighting future opportunities for developing reliable and automatic gas detection systems.

papers.title: A Systematic Evaluation Study on Parameter Inference of Gene Regulatory Networks via Physics-Informed Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Inferring parameters of gene regulatory networks from time-series data is challenging due to non-convexity and poor identifiability. We propose Gene-PINN, a physics-informed neural network that embeds the governing ODEs into the loss function to jointly learn dynamics and estimate parameters. Systematic evaluation reveals that inhibitory edges and feedback loops trade off data fitting against parameter accuracy, network density has an optimal range, and topologies cluster into distinct identifiability groups. This work systematically characterizes how network structure governs parameter inference, guiding physics-informed machine learning in systems and synthetic biology.

papers.title: A Five-Tier Digital Twin Framework with Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Predictive Battery Management in 5G User Equipment: Joint RAN-Aware Degradation Modeling and Autonomous Power Saving
papers.abstract: The deployment of 5G New Radio (NR) introduces millimeter-wave communications, massive MIMO, and carrier aggregation, which significantly increase the power consumption of user equipment (UE) modems and accelerate lithium-ion battery degradation. Existing Battery Management Systems (BMS) optimize charge/discharge cycles without awareness of radio access network (RAN) traffic patterns, while the RAN configures Discontinuous Reception (DRX) and Bandwidth Part (BWP) parameters without knowledge of the battery’s State of Health (SoH). This paper proposes DT-5GBat, a five-tier Digital Twin framework that closes this gap by integrating a physics-informed neural network (PINN) with a 5G network simulator for predictive, cross-layer battery management. Tier 1 provides a reduced-order Single Particle Model (SPM) of the Li-ion cell. Tier 2 fuses real-time BMS sensor data with RAN metrics (RSRP, CQI, RRC state, DRX duty cycle). Tier 3 employs a PINN-LSTM architecture to predict SoH trajectory and Remaining Useful Life (RUL). Tier 4 solves a multi-objective optimization problem trading off energy consumption, latency, and battery aging. Tier 5 executes the optimized policy in a closed control loop via UE middleware or O-RAN RIC. It is validated by co-simulation between NS-3/5G-LENA and the Rakhmatov non-linear battery model using NASA Ames, Oxford, and CALCE datasets augmented with synthetic 5G load traces. DT-5GBat extends UE autonomy by 21.3% and reduces capacity fade by 19.8% over 500 equivalent cycles, with a RUL prediction MAPE of 3.42% and a computational overhead below 1.8% of the total UE energy budget.

papers.title: Learning, simulation, and reasoning for decision making in complex dynamical systems
papers.abstract: Abstract Many complex systems of scientific and societal importance, including epidemics, energy grids, transportation networks, and supply chains, are governed by nonlinear dynamics, are only partially observed through noisy and heterogeneous data, and are continuously reshaped by interventions. These properties make decision making fundamentally challenging, particularly when the mechanisms driving system behavior are only partially understood. While modern machine learning has achieved remarkable predictive performance, real‐world applications require AI systems that combine forecasting with uncertainty quantification, counterfactual reasoning, intervention analysis, and mechanism‐aware reasoning. This article synthesizes my line of work on learning, simulation, and reasoning in complex dynamical systems. Using epidemic prediction and decision making as a running example, I describe recent advances that illustrate the growing integration of data‐driven learning, scientific simulation, and mechanistic reasoning, and discuss how these complementary paradigms can support forecasting, intervention analysis, and high‐stakes decision making.

papers.title: Metodologias ativas na educação infantil: possibilidades para o desenvolvimento da linguagem escrita por meio de experiências significativas
papers.abstract: Early Childhood Education constitutes a fundamental stage of Basic Education, characterized by the centrality of interactions, play, and experiences that foster children's holistic development. In this context, engagement with written language should not be understood merely as a precursor to formal literacy processes, but rather as an opportunity for children to participate in social reading and writing practices. Concurrently, active learning methodologies have gained prominence in educational discourse for valuing student participation, inquiry, collaboration, problem-solving, creative production, and agency. This study aims to analyze, through a bibliographic review, how active learning methodologies can contribute to the development of written language in Early Childhood Education, considering play, games, projects, inquiry, literature, and collective productions as meaningful experiences of engagement with written culture. The study is qualitative and basic in nature, with exploratory and descriptive objectives, conducted through bibliographic research and an integrative literature review. The discussion is grounded in the work of authors such as Vygotsky (2007), Ferreiro and Teberosky (1999), Kishimoto (2011), Soares (2006), Moran (2018), Bacich and Moran (2018), Araujo (2017; 2020), Albuquerque and Ferreira (2020), Sombrio and Pereira (2022), Reis and Amiel (2023), Maia and Dórea (2024), Faria, Silva, and Carvalho (2025), and Paixão and Tassoni (2026), as well as relevant Brazilian regulatory documents. The results of the bibliographic analysis indicate that active learning methodologies can foster meaningful experiences of engagement with written culture when aligned with the characteristics of childhood, playfulness, social interactions, and intentional teacher mediation. It is concluded that the contribution of these methodologies lies not in automatically producing literacy, but in creating contexts in which children can use, explore, interpret, and reinterpret written language in socially meaningful situations.

papers.title: Surrogate-Model-Based Simulation and Management of Seawater Intrusion: Progress, Challenges, and Outlook
papers.abstract: Abstract Seawater intrusion (SWI) remains a major challenge in the management of coastal aquifers. Although high-fidelity variably-density flow and transport models can accurately represent SWI processes, their computational cost limits their use in multi-scenario optimization, uncertainty quantification, and risk assessment. To address this limitation, surrogate modeling approaches have increasingly been adopted, aiming to approximate the input-output relationships of complex SWI models at substantially lower cost. This paper reviews recent advances in surrogate models for SWI simulation and management and proposes a classification framework based on the degree of physics integration and the adopted dimensionality-reduction strategy. Existing approaches are categorized into five groups: data-driven models, physics-integrated models, multi-fidelity models, reduced-order models, and neural operators. Furthermore, the coupling strategies between surrogate models and pumping-optimization frameworks (e.g., genetic algorithms, particle swarm optimization, Bayesian optimization) are examined, together with their roles in supporting multi-objective pumping management and uncertainty analysis.

papers.title: Steady Path: Ensuring Stability in Autonomous Industrial Maneuvering
papers.abstract: Autonomous Industrial Vehicles (AIVs) operating in warehouses and industrial facilities must navigate constrained layouts while responding to stationary and moving obstacles.A path that is geometrically collision-free may still produce undesirable motion if vehicle dynamics and terminal behavior are not considered during control.This paper presents SteadyPath, a simulation-based framework for stability-aware autonomous industrial maneuvering.The framework combines a virtual perception layer based on simulator-generated ground-truth object positions and distances, vehicle-state estimation, obstacle-aware decision-making, A* path planning, and Model Predictive Control with terminal constraints.The MPC controller predicts future vehicle motion over a finite horizon and selects steering and longitudinal control actions while seeking a stable terminal condition.The system is evaluated using four scenario tests and a quantitative comparison against a baseline controller.In the reported mission benchmark, the proposed controller completed the mission in 76.4 s compared with 85.6 s for the baseline, reduced mean tracking error from 14.61 m to 2.52 m, reduced peak lateral deviation from 18.91 m to 5.25 m, and increased the clearance buffer margin from 1.30 m to 3.60 m.Both controllers recorded zero dynamic detours or re-plans in the benchmark.The proposed controller was recorded as reaching an invariant stable terminal set, while the baseline was recorded as having a lagging boundary.Scenario testing showed successful outcomes for normal-road, static-obstacle, and fully blocked-road cases; the moving-obstacle case requires clarification because its textual result says the obstacle was handled safely while its status is marked FAIL.The findings indicate improved performance on the reported simulation metrics, while further testing is required to establish robustness across broader dynamic conditions and real sensor inputs.

papers.title: Rapid Wind-load Prediction for a Standard Tall Building Using Physics-informed Deep Learning and CFD Surrogate Modelling
papers.abstract: Abstract An accurate estimation of wind loads applied on tall buildings is still a challenge for civil engineers. Traditionally performed CFD simulations are computationally expensive enough to be unaffordable for use in the iterative process of design. A framework that exploits a physics-informed deep learning method is hereby proposed that performs fast wind pressure estimations for tall buildings. It will be demonstrated for one geometry through a proof-of-concept study of the CAARC standard tall building. The main principle relies on injecting information on the governing physical laws, in the shape of a physics-informed loss term, into a neural network for training. In this new learning model, the loss is made up by the Navier-Stokes equation itself and not solely on the numerical output of the CFD simulation to ensure physicsconsistent predictions during learning. An investigation scenario using the CAARC standard tall building as a case study is presented, and a physics-informed neural network trained on 11,520 points over several wind directions and with several turbulence models showed that the accuracy of prediction of the coefficient of determination (R) was 0.989, 0.986, 0.942 and 0.918 for pressure and U, V and W velocities, inference times below 0.01 s (4–5 orders of magnitude less than typical CFD simulations) and the result simultaneously incorporated both physically consistent predictions and conservation laws. For the test case presented, a Cd of 0.686 is estimated in line with values for the typical rectangular aerodynamic shape profile. It will be concluded that the proposed strategy would be very promising for estimating wind load on this CAARC building geometry but that future research is warranted for training PINNs that estimate wind load upon varying building geometries.

papers.title: A database of interactive plant anatomy images as a teaching platform for plant and wood anatomy
papers.abstract: Summary In recent decades, instruction in plant anatomy has declined due to reduced laboratory time, high maintenance costs, and a decreasing number of trained specialists. At the same time, efforts to digitize anatomical collections have expanded, although static images fail to capture the exploratory experience of microscopy. To address this limitation, we developed a lightweight, browser-based database of interactive plant anatomical micrographs. The system uses scalable vector graphics (SVG) to define tissue regions as dynamic, labelled “hotspots” that respond to cursor movement, enabling intuitive exploration of anatomical structures. Each image is a self-contained file with embedded annotations, allowing easy distribution and integration into teaching and research. The database was constructed in a modular format aligned with teaching laboratory topics, specifically wood anatomy and wood identification including annotated sections of stems, roots and leaves from representative monocot and dicot species. Initial evaluation by laboratory instructors and students indicated improved clarity, engagement, and perceived educational value, particularly due to the combination of high-resolution imagery and interactive labelling. Unlike conventional virtual microscopy platforms, this approach requires no specialized infrastructure or large datasets, making it broadly accessible and easy to implement. This work demonstrates a practical framework for transforming traditional slide collections into interactive digital resources that support active learning, laboratory preparation, and cross-institutional collaboration in plant anatomy education and research.

papers.title: Structural Reliability Analysis Based on Active Learning Gaussian Process Regression
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Maintaining high prediction accuracy in structural reliability analysis under limited computational budgets and a limited number of high‐cost function evaluations remains a significant challenge. To address this issue, an active learning Gaussian process regression (AGPR) method is proposed for reliability assessment. The proposed method improves the quality and spatial distribution of the initial training samples, enabling more effective use of limited computational resources and reducing the influence of redundant samples on surrogate model construction. Furthermore, the surrogate model is adaptively refined in critical regions associated with failure probability estimation, allowing more accurate characterization of the limit‐state boundary with a limited number of function evaluations. By improving the representativeness of training samples and refining the surrogate model near the limit‐state boundary, the proposed method can provide accurate failure probability estimates with a limited number of function evaluations. Numerical and engineering examples indicate that the proposed method can achieve accurate failure probability estimates with fewer function evaluations than several existing approaches in the considered examples. These results indicate the potential of the proposed method for structural reliability analysis under limited computational budgets.

papers.title: Closed-Loop Wheelbase-Preview Model Predictive Control for Active Suspension Using Reconstructed Road Information
papers.abstract: This study presents a closed-loop wheelbase-preview model predictive control (MPC) method for vehicle pitch-attitude regulation during localized bump traversal without a forward-looking road sensor. Road information reconstructed from front unsprung-mass acceleration supports front-axle compensation and causal rear-axle preview. An existing linear–quadratic static output feedback (LQSOF) controller supplies the baseline force, while MPC optimizes an additional rear command using predictions of future feedback action and actuator dynamics. CarSim–MATLAB/Simulink co-simulations evaluate performance at 20, 30, and 40 km/h. Relative to LQSOF, the complete configuration reduces the pitch-angle RMS by 9.5–17.5% and the pitch-rate RMS by 18.9–24.3%, without uniform improvement in vertical acceleration. Relative to front compensation alone, rear MPC further reduces the pitch-angle RMS by 16.0% and 11.8% at 20 and 30 km/h, but this benefit is not maintained at 40 km/h. A proportional rear-gain sweep identifies condition-dependent trade-offs between pitch regulation, vertical response, and actuator demand. Controlled ablation and sensitivity analyses characterize the prediction-model components and disturbance dependence. Unsuccessful constrained optimization at 50 and 60 km/h limits the current implementation; no incremental high-speed MPC benefit over LQSOF is established.

papers.title: 27 Al + ion optical clock with a fractional systematic uncertainty of 4.8 × 10 − 19
papers.abstract: We report the development and evaluation of a quantum logic spectroscopy based 25 Mg + − 27 Al + ion optical clock with a fractional systematic uncertainty of 4.8 × 10 − 19 . Multiple improvements are reported. The population leakage accumulation among Zeeman sublevels of the 25 Mg + ion hyperfine ground states during Raman sideband cooling is analyzed, enabling an optimal determination of the DC bias magnetic field. We also perform a direct measurement of the RF induced AC magnetic field in three directions. The quadratic Zeeman coefficient for the 1 S 0 ↔︎ 3 P 0 transition of 27 Al + ion is measured to be 𝐶 2 = −71.914(11) Hz/mT 2 . The quadratic Zeeman shift uncertainty is reduced by a factor of more than five without significant influence on the Raman sideband cooling of the ion pair. The three orthogonal Raman laser beam paths are optimized, enabling longer coherence time to suppress and evaluate the excess micromotion in three spatial directions. The demonstrated 27 Al + optical clock offers a reliable platform for future redefinition of the SI “second”.

papers.title: Adaptive Control of HVAC Systems in Public Buildings Under Dense Crowds: A Review of Synergistic Strategies for Thermal Comfort and Energy Saving
papers.abstract: Rapid changes in crowd occupancy create coupled sensible, latent, and ventilation loads that challenge HVAC operation in public buildings. This narrative review synthesizes research on dynamic load mismatch, occupancy sensing and forecasting, adaptive control, and coordinated precooling and demand response. The reviewed evidence indicates that effective regulation requires joint management of cooling, moisture removal, and ventilation. Multi-source sensing can improve occupancy information, although CO2-based estimation remains sensitive to air exchange, mixing, and response time. Forecasting is most useful when advance action can exploit thermal storage or prevent operating constraints from being violated; simple occupancy-feedback control remains a relevant comparator. Model predictive control and reinforcement learning offer opportunities for coordinated optimization, but their benefits depend on model quality, operating conditions, and control baselines. Evidence from offices, simulations, and controlled experiments provides methodological guidance, while deployment in densely occupied public spaces requires field validation addressing forecast uncertainty, transient thermal comfort, ventilation requirements, and equipment constraints.
